rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE or correctness failures, so this round raises obfuscation pressure across the board: SUB, BCF, and FLA get high SecurityGain weights since the workload is dominated by a few numeric kernels (deflat, main, allroots, newton) where bogus control flow and flattening meaningfully disrupt static recovery of the root-finding loops, and their small text size (~2.4KB total) means size growth from BCF/FLA is acceptable, hence mid-range SizeCost tolerances. RuntimeCost weights are set moderate rather than low: allroots is a compute benchmark with iterative root-solving loops, so BCF and FLA in the hot inner loops (HORNERS, newton) still carry real overhead and should not be maximally forced, while SPLIT, IBR, IGV, and ICALL get raised DiversityGain weights because they compose well — SPLIT creates more basic blocks for FLA/BCF to scramble, IBR obscures the flattened dispatcher edges, and ICALL hides the small call graph among the 7 functions. CorrectnessRisk weights stay below 0.5 everywhere to preserve the clean round-1 result, with SUB and ICALL kept slightly lower-risk-tolerant since arithmetic substitution and indirect calls on floating-point-heavy code are the likeliest spots for subtle numeric or ABI-adjacent breakage.
